This contest is an idea I just thought up, in the map, the rules are.

1) The enemy has to be standing still, no moving enemies allowed ( homing launchers allowed ).

2) There must be only one enemy.

3) The map can be as big as you want it.

4) mines count as enemies ( 10 mines = 1 normal enemy )

5) Score is worked out like this:

Playability(P): /10
Map design(MD): /5
Enemy use(EU): /5
Enjoyability(E): /10

Overall score(OS): /30

6) Judges are:

me, chasethebase
Clovic
Guiseppi
open for nomination

7) start date is on the 15th of march, end on the 20th of march

GOOD LUCK!!

P.S. for a demonstration on which enemy to use, look here, http://numa.notdot.net/map/30471

Nature (N) : 30

N: 41
F: 35
E:10

Total: 86/110

fun, but there are a lot of un-nessecary objects on the map, unless it is cheatable, or you have the choice for all gold...

N: 40
F: 35
E: 9
Total: 84/110

fun. the rockets reduce your chances of survial greatly, and also prove to be a pain in the ****, so that means you lose points for that...

Brave the Coming Tide by PALEMOON

N: 45
F: 40
E: 7
Total: 92/110

Kornfield by Zacko

N: 42
F: 38
E: 7

Veolciraptor by nemetacyst

N: 45
F: 40
E: 10

Total: 95/110

Petals of demise by walrus_of_death

F: 37
E: 7

good, yet simple, and easy to make, but the slight problem is the enemy placement, which hinders your chances of winning...

Dark Waters by walrus_of_death

F: 40
E: 8

Total: 88/110

good and interesting, very fun and challenging...

Butterphish by nemetacyst

N: 46
F: 39
E: 10

Total: 95/110

Great tileset, but let down by the amount of switches needed to press...

  • The judge then posts the scores from the 2 demos once both are recieved.

#213272 77 2006-08-08T20:03:43Z Chase
Judging from me:

Zugbop 1

Design: 7/10
Style: 6/10
Effort: 7/10
Total: 20/30

Well done, is similar to the current banner, keeping with the current look, but the 3D ninja gives it a new, unique look, if the 3D ninja was created in a program such as Photoshop, I can guess how this would look, but the cartoony, paint style is cool as well.

Evil___

Design: 7/10
Style: 7/10
Effort: 7/10
Total: 21/30

Nice colour scheme, but I think there are too many ninjas which makes the banner look cluttered, the single blue ninja shown in your work in progress banner was better, in my opinion, adding the gold bar made it look slightly better.

Dark Ball Y-E

Design: 5/10
Style: 6/10
Effort: 6/10
Total: 17/30

Ok, the colour scheme doesn't really suit Metanet, reducing your Style score, the ninja's pose is good though, but a few points I would like to mention are the text, logo and the overall quality of the image, the text had rough edges, pointing to a coloured box being placed over each line of the letters. The logo was off the colour of the original, which meant you lost points for design, and the quality was poor, with rough edges and scruffy fills. You could try harder, just to me it seems this was a 5 minute job, it is best to take your time to get it right (No offence).

Borealis

Design: 8/10
Style: 9/10
Effort: 8/10
Total: 25/30

Well Done, I like the style of the Banner, it goes with the current colour scheme of the forum, it is a shame that you put the wrong website on the banner though, the ninja is a bit rough around the edges, so a colour overlay combined with a stroke of 1 pixel (If you have Photoshop) can sure this problem. Overall this is a banner of very high standards and it looks perfect, has potential to replace the current banner.

Zugbop 2

Design: 7/10
Style: 7/10
Effort: 8/10
Total: 22/30

I like the colour of the banner, it is a bit dark though so I dislike that, but it works well, I like this one a lot, the text is a bit rough though, which is a shame, because if you had chosen a different font and made it smoother, this would be brilliant!

July comes around and I have organised the N League, which was a great contest, which lasted until October, but the people dis-continued to play after August...I had become a lot better at making sigs and had a lot of friends in the community...I also began to use IRC at this point

#12328 1 2006-11-17T18:11:00Z Chase
Here is your one stop shop for reviews of games, which will be of games posted here and commercial games, if you want a game to be reviewed, just post your request here...

The Team[/u]
Chasethebase
Mysterypower
BritanniaWD
Twistkill
Ninjapants
Luminaflare
RincewindSW

Reviews Done[/u]
N (Chasethebase)
The Snowball Fighter (Keron Cyst)
Need for Speed: Most Wanted (BritanniaWD)
Soldat (RincewindSW)
Counter Strike Source (Chasethebase)

But there is only one starting place, N

Quote
N[/u]

Can this game live up to its community following? I will review this and find out

Going back many years, there was a game called Lode Runner, a few may have heard of it, some may not, but it was a brilliant game in its own right, being addicting and challenging at the same time. Then there is now, 2006, and we have N, it is based off Lode Runner and you can see the similarities, but N is also a lot different to its ancestor, there are multiple tile shapes, making levels more diverse and different, there are many enemy types and objects, which also provide a greater challenge. This game is easily addictive and it is hard at the same time, providing a challenge to pretty much everyone. Its current version, 1.4 is the best yet, with refined physics, a level editor and less glitches, it is almost unbeatable, but obviously is, due to version 1.5 being released in the near future.

Graphics & Sound

Ns graphics arent much to shout about, it is a two-dimensional game set in a grey world, but look closely and everything seems crisp and clear, there are no blurs, no loose pixels and no sharp pixelated edges, making this a beautiful game to look at too. Sounds in the game seem in depth, they are sharp, like the graphics, but also provide feeling to the game, when your character dies, there is a sharp, crunching sound of the bones breaking in the players body, and everything literally falling to pieces, due to the physics in the game, which I will come to later.

Playability

N is a vast game, with a good 500 levels in the Main Game alone, included with the game upon download are approximately 200 User Made levels in one file, which are loaded into the game, this makes 700 levels bundled with the game already, but you can expand this, to this very point, there are another 68334 maps available from NUMA, The N User Map Archive, to which people submit maps for the world to see, play and rate. But that isnt all, on the forums, people have started to make level packs, which provide another few hundred levels to play, so you can never get bored of it.

Physics

Now here is where N really starts to show its strengths, it has rag doll physics used for the player, meaning when the player dies, the body becomes limp and flops around like, as the name suggests, a rag doll, this provides reality to the game, with the fun of watching the dead body being flung around the level from coming into contact with enemies.

Verdict

N is a great game in its own right, but a few things are yet to be improved, as version 1.5 is to be released, that should clear up any problems this current version has. For a game made in Flash, it is huge, and must have required a vast amount of ActionScript and coding, as well as a long period of time. Credit from this goes to Mare and Raigan, who made this game; it is a truly brilliant game, and best of luck with version 1.5!

+ Amazing physics
+ Number of levels
+ Level of difficulty is not too hard, but provides a challenge
+ The number of tricks to learn also spans miles
- Slight stutter on slopes and chances of survival in certain death situations

Final Verdict: 93%

Very good, still slight room for improvement, but overall a brilliant game that lasts hours upon hours.

#273478 4 2006-12-19T18:55:50Z Chase
Ok, detailed answer coming up...

Nintendo are a good games company, they make their own games as well as having third party support, the Wii and DS are attracting the whole market available, and this is successfully raking in the money. The games they make are unique, Zelda, Mario, Metroid to name a few, are all a twist on the traditional genres they are made on/made themselves. Nintendo defined gaming, and will continue to do so.

Microsoft are doing incredibly well, with a year ahead of the rest in this generation of gaming, and with the Xbox 360's HD compatabilities, Microsoft have been very successful, with games like Sonic the Hedgehog and Viva Pinata out, they are trying very hard to attract everyone to their console, but it isn't working, due to the fact that it is still a bunch of complicated buttons to people of an older generation. They are good at what they do, but not good enough to persuade me.

Sony...they have just ruined their chances this generation, trying to stuff too much into the PS3, a Blu-Ray player, who needs that? The PS3 may have amazing graphics, but they can't get much better, so they have had to find a load of new fancy gadgetry to attract people. Leaving the release to this late will lose them the war this time, I am refering to Europe here BTW. But they have messed up big time.

Looks like the only competitors here are Microsoft and Nintendo, and Nintendo seem to be winning...so they get my vote, as I own a Wii and a DS Lite, this may seem biased, but it isn't, as I was attracted by the 360 at one point, and if GAME did a similar offer to the 'Buy Zelda:TP for the Gamecube and get a free Pre-owned one' for the old Xbox, I'd buy one, because the games rocked!

#276002 62 2006-12-23T20:49:54Z Chase
Ok, finally the review is done, I will add images soon, but for now I have the review!

===========

Counter Strike Source


This game is only Counter Strike 1.6 on top of the Source engine, do the fancy graphics make it a better game overall, lets see

This game is based on multiplayer warfare, between two teams, the Counter Terrorists (CTs) and the Terrorists (Ts). You may think that you will only be playing Online, yes, you are, but you can play against bots if you want to practice.


A terrorist running away, from what I wonder?

At the start of any match, you have a small pistol and a knife, you have to buy weapons with the cash you have. You earn cash by winning games, even if you die, if the team wins, you get more cash. There is a special pricing system in the game, so that the prices of weapons will change from week to week, and from server to server, so you may pay $1000 for something, and then pay $2000 the next week. The CTs get different weapons from the Ts, so if you want a weapon the other team gets, you have to drop your weapon and pick up theirs, once you have killed them of course. You can only buy weapons from buy zones, you find out if you are in one or not by the green trolley symbol tha appears on the left of your monitor.


The buy menu in the rifles section, what to choose...

The maps are all different, you get realistic maps, and you get VR maps, you get surf maps, which I will explain later on, and some user created maps, each providing different scenery and different sniping points. Also you can get different tasks on each map, some maps have bombsites which the Ts aim to plant their bomb at, if they are successful, the CTs have to defuse it before it explodes. Or there is the basic eliminate all enemies deathmatch mode, or you can try to rescue the hostages, where CTs have to make it to the hostages, and return them to the hostage rescue point, without losing any en-route. The surf maps are deathmatches, but they usually consist of long prism shaped ramps, which you have to slide along by holding either strafe key, so you stay on, for example, if A and D are your strafe keys, left and right respectively, you would move like so.
D /\ A. Here, you hold the left strafe to keep on the slope on the right side.


One of the more realistic maps in the game.

Weapons come under 5 categories and an equipment category; there are Pistols, Shotguns, SMGs, Rifles and Machine Guns, the equipment category contains grenades, armour, defusal kits and night vision. So you have plenty to buy. The combination of weapons you carry can also be chosen tactically, choose a sniper and a strong pistol, choose a strong SMG and a weak pistol, there are many combinations, each having it's advantages and disadvantages in maps. Also in the game, when you, or any opponent dies, the body goes limp, using ragdoll physics, similar to the ones N uses. This means that you can shoot the body, and it will flop around everywhere, creating many opportunities for mild humour.


An example of the physics, it seems the character was shot from the front and fell back

Each side has 4 custom characters to choose from, the CTs have people from different armies across the world, the British SAS, the SEAL Team 6 from America, The GSG 9 from Germany and the GIGN from France. The Terrorists have 4 people from different terrorist groups, each looking somewhat stupid in their own right. Another point of the game is the spray option, you can graffiti the map you are on in game, but the graffiti gets removed over time, or when you spraypaint somewhere else. You can use a pre-set spray, or upload a custom one, meaning all sorts of pictures get used (Dont get any ideas!).


One of the standard spays, which has a clear outline so it blends into the terrain behind it.

Most servers in the game use VAC, which stands for VALVe Anti-Cheat, this prevents cheaters getting away with what they do and banning them, some hacking programs can not be detected by this, but the system keeps getting updated to block the newer hacks. The servers can be filtered so you can find exactly what you want, for example, you may want to play on the map de_dust2, so you type in the map box the map you want, and it finds all servers currently playing on that map, making the game overall much more enjoyable.

Just another recent addition are the mods, these are twists on the main gameplay modes that opens up new ways to play, the only mod I have noticed so far is the ZombieMod, where there are two teams, one team has all the humans on it, while the other has one zombie. The zombies have different character designs too, making them unique. But the main difference is the overall gameplay and stats, if a zombie kills a human, they turn into a zombie and their screen becomes green, they move quicker and have a absurd amount of Hp, while the humans have little Hp, they have infinite ammunition, so they shouldn't worry about being killed so easily.


A screen of what it's like to be a zombie...

Counter Strike Source is all about the multiplayer, if you want a game with a strong single player campaign, buy Call of Duty, but if you want fun, up to date warfare, where you can play against your friends, this is the game to buy!

+ Multiplayer is addictive.
+ Source engine creates realistic graphics.
+ Choice of weapons gives greater enjoyment.
+ Some mods change the overall gameplay.
- Some textures don't load and become ugly purple and black check patterns.

Final Verdict: 87%

Good game, fun for a while, but eventually the lack of single player campaign will deter buyers and reduce replay factor. This game is replayable, but good for the odd while once you have become bored with it.

==========

After the delay, it's finally done, hope you like it!

#279686 64 2007-01-01T15:04:10Z Chase
=======

Wii Play

For an extra 5 you can get a copy of Wii Play with a Wii Remote, is it worth the added cost?

Wii Play is made up of 9 smaller games which all use the Wii Remote in a different way. When you start you only have access to one game, but once you have played the first game you get access to the next game and so on (regardless of success) until you have unlocked all nine. I will go into more detail with the games later on, but for now I will explain the main features of Wii Play itself. Wii Play is for up to two players, meaning that you are more likely to pass the remote around between a group of three or more. The compatibility with your Miis is also a fun addition to the game, meaning you can play as yourself (or as close as you can get to make the Mii look like you) in the games.



The first game available is shooting. In a duck hunt esque style, you have to shoot all the targets, or as many as possible. These targets range from clay pigeons to UFOs that try to abduct your Miis. During multiplayer, the UFO stage has 6 Miis, which normally are all yours, but they are split 3:3 between the players. If you try to save yours and let theirs get abducted, you will gain more bonus points at the end. The ducks from Duck Hunt make an appearance each round giving the opportunity for bonus points, if you can shoot them.



Upon completing a round of shooting you unlock Find Mii, this game does as it says on the tin. You have to find the Miis that the game tells you to. The Miis will be doing a set activity and you have to find the ones specified by the game. Sometimes it will be the one you are using, sometimes it will be the look-alikes. In later stages of the game you have to use the Wii Remote like a flashlight to find your specified Miis in the crowd, adding enough variety to last a good 20 minutes.



Next is Table Tennis, you are required to move the remote to move the paddle on screen so it hits the ball. All the rules of normal table tennis apply here, from serving to obstructions. In multiplayer it is the first player to obtain 11 points, while in single player mode you have to rally for as long as possible, but the game stops at 100, so you will eventually have 5 high scores of 100.



The game after this is probably the most difficult and least entertaining here. Pose Mii requires the player to move the Mii on screen and change the pose it sits in to match the one in the bubble. In the later stages of the game you can find yourself missing bubbles and it becomes frantic. If you miss a bubble and it falls to the bottom, you get a miss, after three misses your game is over. In multiplayer, the colour of the pose is essential, if you see a red bubble falling to the bottom and you are P1, you can leave that as P2 is red in the multiplayer mode of the game.



The fifth game you unlock is laser hockey, which is similar to pong. You have to score as many points as you can in single player mode, and the lead you have over the CPU player is your final score. In multiplayer mode the first player to reach eight points is the winner. If you twist the remote upon impact with the puck, you can send it flying a different direction across the table.



Next in line is one of the best games in Wii Play. Pool is fairly difficult to start with, but once you have grasped the controls it is good fun for everyone. The objective is to pot the balls in order, you have to hit the target ball first; this means potting other balls afterwards is not classed as a foul, but fouls deduct points from your final score. To hit the ball, you have to pull the Wii Remote back while holding B, then push the Wii Remote forward to hit the ball; still holding B until the ball has been hit.



Fishing is fun, but it requires a lot of patience. You have to catch the fish by swinging the Wii Remote back once a fish has bitten (The Wii Remotes speaker will let you know if one has). You can gain bonus points by catching the specific fish shown at the top of the screen. Some fish subtract points from your total, so be careful.



Charge is a game where your Mii rides a cow and tries to knock down scarecrows. Holding the Wii Remote sideways, you tilt it forward to make it move faster and tilt it back to make the cow slow down. To jump fences you have to quickly lift the Wii Remote up.



The last game in Wii Play is Tanks. Here you control a small tank (Blue for P1 and Red for P2) with the D-Pad or the Nunchuk attachment. Pressing the B trigger fires shells that bounce of walls once. The aim is to destroy all tanks on the board to progress to the next level. The enemy tanks vary in capabilities that are shown by the colour of their tanks. There is little depth to this game, but it is fun while it lasts.

Looking at the whole game, it does what it intends to do, it teaches how to use the Wii Remote. The graphics style looks good and fresh and the game lasts forever. It lacks in single player, but multiplayer is where this game truly shines; for a fiver extra you cant go far wrong!

+Variety of games is superb
+Controls are simple to master
+Multiplayer creates longetivity
+Value for money
-Table tennis is a letdown.

Final Score: 91%

=======

Relevance ?/5 This is how relevant the image is to the theme.
Effort ?/5 How much time and effort was put into this image.

Style ?/5 How the content works with itself

  • You submit your images to Chasethebase using the forum's integrated Personal Message function. Please do not use CODE or QUOTE to separate the image data. Just copy & paste it!

#13505 1 2007-01-13T18:25:19Z Chase
OK, after having seen all three next-gen consoles in action, it's time to release my verdict on which is most likely to win the war. This will be an unbiased opinion.

Nintendo Wii
Lets start with the one I own, the Wii is an exceptional console, which lacks power, but has many other capabilities to make up for it. The most important of this being the Wii's remote, which shocked most people upon revelation. Control systems using this feel much more realistic, compared to beefed up graphics using a typical games controller. The downsides are the fact that bluetooth can really mess up the remote and the sensor bar, also most of the main features are only accessible with a wireless internet connection, or having a Nintendo Wi-Fi USB Connector; costing around 25. The games available for this console are truly superb; The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess is the main title for the Wii's release, and it won over most people from the PS2's generation. Red Steel is the main FPS for the console, with Call of Duty III following close behind. My final opinion of the console is great, it rocks, it gives an exhilirating experience that cannot be matched.

Microsoft Xbox 360
The release of the 360 one year ago tempted me a lot, this made me think wether or not to buy this now to get my fix of Nex-Gen gaming, or wait until the 'Revolution' came out. I chose the latter, and the name change didn't put me off. Back to the 360; the main appeal is Xbox Live, this is the best online gaming system for consoles at the moment, even surpassing Nintendo's Wi-Fi system; it has a downside though, cost. You have to pay to use Xbox Live; it's worth it though, with games like Halo 3 on the horizon, this looks to be a promising year for Microsoft. Consoles bought recently will have had the overheating problem solved (I hope), but early consoles shut down because of the temperature rise. Another downside is the Premium/Core packages, you may think that you get a better deal getting the Core package and a Hard Drive; this is a bad idea, get the Premium package so you also get the chrome disk tray. The nicest idea was the face plates, they can make your Xbox unique to you, so I would advise getting one.

Sony Playstation 3
At the time of writing, this console has yet to be released in the UK, so I have had the priviledge of seeing one in action. This console has a few downsides, the Blu-Ray disks may never be popular; making this a risk. Also the price is astonishing, 500-600 is a lot of money that some people may not be able to afford. But this console is worth the price, the most expensive console with the 60Gb hard drive is about 600, but looking at the graphics and power it can churn out, it looks truly amazing. If you want your fix of proper next-gen games, this is where it's at. The price and lack of immense launch titles may put buyers off, but in the future this may seem like a purchase worth its cost. The style of the console looks really groovy too, which I like, the size and weight (5kg) mean moving it about is hard work, but they are not really downsides to the console.

After looking in depth at all three consoles, my verdict is that the Wii will come out victorious if Nintendo keeps bringing out good unique games for it. It still has games for the die hard gamer, while new, unique games will attract new buyers. DS compatability is also a high point for the console, and Pokmon Battle Revolution seems to be it's Joker. People think it will be bad, as it's Pokmon, but it is leading the way with DS Connectivity and Wi-Fi. The Xbox 360 will be it's main rival, but unfortunately the PS3 will lack with sales because of it's price. Wait a while and the PS3's price will crash, like the PSP's did, it looks brilliant, and I love it, but I just wouldn't buy one.

Ok, I'm going to explain this, it runs similar to the system on Newgrounds.

When you submit a map, it becomes under judgement, here any viewer has several options.
  • To blow the whistle to say it is stolen material
  • To rate and comment on the map
After judgement, depending on the map's ratings, it will either be deleted or saved. The map stays in the User's own maps page, but is deleted from the whole site's records and does not affect the User's map count.

Voting during this stage may only be available to certain members to prevent the sniping issue continuing.

Discuss.

Spoiler: Clauses
Species Clause
A species clause is a restriction on the number of same Pokemon you can use. If a species clause is in play, then you can only use one of each Pokemon in your team. So no teams of 3 Scythers and 3 Arcanines.

Item Clause
An item clause limits the number of same items allowed to be held by the Pokemon. For example if it is in play then you may only have 1 Leftovers item being held by a Pokemon.

Type Clause
A type clause would be used to stop you from using Pokemon of a specific type. Though rarely used, may be put in place by a Leader to make it a slightly fairer match. For example a Fighting Type clause being enforced by the Dark type Gym Leader.

We will allow the usage of Type Clause but to make it fair a few rules were put in place:
You can clause only one type
Pokemon of dual types are not allowed in the Gym. For example if Dark Type Pokemon were claused, then a Houndoom or Tyranitar would not be allowed.

Sleep Clause
Very common clause which stops people from mass Hypnotising entire teams. This limits the opponent to only put one Pokemon to sleep at a time. If affected Pokemon faints, you can put another Pokemon to sleep.

Burn Clause
Hard to actually enforce, but the idea is simple. The opponent can only use Will-o-wisp succesfully on only one Pokemon at a time. If affected Pokemon is fainted, WoW can be used again. Unintentional burn from attacking moves does not count.

Para Clause
Same as the burn clause. The oponent can only use Thunder Wave or Stun Spore succesfully on only one Pokemon at a time. If affected Pokemon is fainted, the moves can be used again. Unintentional paralysis from attacking moves does not count.

Poison Clause
Same as the two above. The oponent can only use Poison Powder, Toxic and Poison Gas successfully on only one Pokemon at a time. If affected Pokemon is fainted, the moves can be used again. Unintentional poison from attacking moves does not count.

The gyms should now be open for challengers to face them when they want. If your gym is not quite ready yet, then if a challenger has beaten the other 7 gyms, they may move on to the final 8th gym. If your gym is inactive for more than a week then I will replace you. You have been warned.

Thank you for your time.

#17205 1 2007-09-13T16:02:41Z Chase

Q: Right, I'm reading this now thinking "What the hell is this about?"
A: First off, if you don't remember the first, I'll explain. This is a competition which brings all the image makers of this forum together. People will be making images using Photoshop, Paint Shop Pro, GIMP, MS Paint, everything they can get their hands on to enter this competition. Some categories might be harder for certain people to complete than others, but the window is open for everyone of every skill level.

Q: How do I enter?
A: You make an image (Duh!) and send it via to me! Me and a special weekly guest will judge the results between ourselves, and post seperate scores. While we are judging, I will post the entries in this thread for the public to see, you can guess which image belongs to who if you wish.

Q: Soo...when does it start?
A: TODAY! Yes, the first week of the competition starts today, and the theme is Freestyle. The guest judge is the grand mod himself, Kashkin.

Q: How are the images scored?
A: The images are scored differently depending on the theme, the overall scoring system is three categories, each scoring ten points each, totalling 30. Adding mine and the guest's scores to create a final total of 60.

Q: Are there any prizes?
A: Yes.

Q: Can you tell us what they are?
A: No. And to save space, because it's a secret.

Q: Any rules?
A: Yes, there are. And I'll list them below:
  • 1 image per person
  • All work should be made on the spot, no past works.
  • If you wish to submit your work to DA, you can, but you'll give away which one is yours.
  • No cheating, my moderating friend Kashkin will check up on this.
  • All images must, as in, MUST be in .PNG format. If you have a problem with this, talk to me about it.
Q: Is that all?
A: Yes, get making!

#18025 1 2007-11-19T18:46:15Z Chase

Welcome to my guide on CS:Source, this will only show you through the basics of playing the game, not installing it, or Steam beforehand.

What the game is exactly...
It's a multiplayer FPS (First person shooter) game, where you join servers of people who will be your opponents. There are two teams, Terrorists and Counter-Terrorists, each gets a different selection of weapons.


Getting to know the controls[/i]
Counter-Strike: Source uses the typical WASD control system, with the keys in a similar layout to the arrow keys. These are for moving around, but not actually aiming, that's what the mouse does, it lets you look around and shoot people. Left clicking fires the weapon, Right clicking uses the Secondary Function (E.g. M4A1 Carbine, adding Silencer), scrolling the mouse wheel will put you in weapon select mode, highlight the weapon you want, and click to change to it.

A couple of extras that'll be necessary...
E = Use, for defusing bombs, opening doors.
Q = Change to last held weapon, so if you had a pistol out, and changed to your rifle, Q would pull the pistol out again.
Ctrl = Crouch, Essential for accuracy, crouching makes it easier to hit people.
Spacebar = Jump, jump around a bit, it's fun! Pressing ctrl while jumping helps you onto higher ledges.
T = Spray, this lets you use your spraypaint image, it 'leaves your mark' on people you killed etc.
F = Flashlight, good for dark levels, press it to switch on, press again to switch off.
Z, X and C = Voice commands, choose a number after pressing one to use that command.
Y = General chat, talk to everyone in the server using this.
U = Team chat, talk to your team only using this.
B = Buy weapons, this lets you get good guns, navigate the buy menu with the mouse or numbers, remember that money doesn't grow on trees, I'll explain how to find out how much you have later.

Right, now the controls are over with, time for the interface...

Image here

Up in the top left is your radar, this will let you find your team mates, but will only show up enemies when you or your friends can visibly see them or are being shot at by them on screen.

Bottom left to bottom right is health, armour, Round time, Ammo (Current Clip | Spare Bullets) and Cash (Above ammo).

Time to explain all the different mods, and a few tips and tricks

Never buy Nightvision, it's useless, and not worth using tbh.

Always buy a Defuse Kit if you're CT, it means it's easier to defuse the bomb.

Zombies!, that'll be the zombie mod, the teams are humans (blue) vs. zombies (red), humans occassionally have infinite ammo, but zombies have around 50x more health and have increased speed, but only a knife.

I can't buy weapons here, and mario sounds are playing!, you're in gungame, the objective here is to kill, and kill some more, so you level up through the weapons. One kill means one level, and knifing gets you a bonus level.

What is this map, it's full of pyramids..., Surfing time! Hold strafe down towards the triangle (D /\ A) and use the mouse to direct yourself. It's good fun.

A few more things[/i]

On de_ maps, the objective is to either plant the bomb (T) or defuse it if it is planted (CT).
On cs_ maps, the objective is to rescue hostages (CT), or stop the CT team (T)

Weapons are usually more expensive depending on popularity or power. A Machine Gun is more expensive than a pistol say.

If you're still confused, send me a PM

P.S. If I missed something, post here and tell me what I should add.

#18307 1 2007-12-07T18:33:44Z Chase
Here is where you find out how to install new custom fonts to Windows XP. Any program which loads fonts, be it Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop or even Microsoft Paint will automatically update. Gimp, if open at the time, will require a click of the refresh button.

Step 1: Finding your font
Websites such as DaFont provide free fonts, but be wary, as some fonts cost to download, so read before you click! Once you find a nice font, click the download button for PC and you're away.

Step 2: Finding your font
This is the easy way of installing your font. Once you've unzipped your file containing the font, open the folder, there should be a file with a O, A or TT on it, letters coloured red, green and blue respectively. Highlight these and select move file from the left pane.

Step 3: Finding the Windows XP Font Directory
A little browse window will pop up. From this click all the - buttons you can see to reduce all open lists to nothing, then click the plus signs next to the following icons, in the following order.
  • C:\ Drive
  • WINDOWS
  • Fonts
Step 4: The finishing touches
Once you select the fonts directory, by highlighting it, click ok, a little window with a progress bar will show up, this is installing your font. Once that's disappeared, you're all done! Just open a program such as Photoshop and experiment!

#18321 1 2007-12-08T19:28:53Z Chase

Welcome to Ninjas - Red vs. Blue

First off, I'll explain the rules.
  • There is a player move 'rota', the players move in order, if one player doesn't respond in 24 hours, he's missed his go. If the player doesn't respond for 3 days, he gets removed.
  • Attacking uses one of 4 moves, 2 equipped weapons, A grenade, or a melee attack.
  • Damage is calculated depending on weapon used, even for melee attack.
  • Once you attack/defend/use an item, you cannot move.
  • Depending on your skill point spend, you can boost skills.
  • You earn skill points per kill.
  • If you die that turn, you will respawn next turn your team has.
  • Weapons are scattered around the map, use them wisely, and change to create killer combos.
  • When you sign up, you don't choose a team, I choose the teams once signup is complete.
  • When signing up, post your skill points spendage, you start with 5 to spend.
Skills
Skills enable you to move farther, do more damage, or jump higher. It all depends on how you spend. The list are as follows.

Power
Speed
Metabolism

One skill point is earned per kill. So choose wisely. Speed is how many tiles you can move, metabolism is how many squares you can jump, and Power is the chance of a critical hit.

Weapons
As is Halo, the weapons are from the games, the weapon selection are from Halo 1 and 2 only. This is due to the lack of sprites Each weapon comes with full ammo, if you die, those weapons disappear off the map. Weapons are as follows.

Plasma Rifle - 100 battery power, loses 1 per 5 bullets fired, loses 10 if overheated, a ratio of 5/10 for overheating. Takes 4 hits to kill.
Plasma Pistol - 100 battery power, loses 1 per 1 bullet, loses 10 per charge bullet, charge takes a turn. Takes 6 hits to kill, or 1 charge and 2 normal.
Beam Rifle - Battery of 100, loses 5 per bullet, 20 lost if overheat. 6/10 chance. Takes two hits to kill.
Fuel Rod Gun - Battery of 100, loses 10 per bullet. Takes 1 hit to kill.
Standard Rifle - Magazine of 60, comes with another 120. Takes 5 hits to kill.
Magnum - Magazine of 6, comes with another 18. Takes 7 hits to kill.
Sniper Rifle - Magazine of 4, comes with another 12, 8x zoom. Takes two hits to kill.
Rocket Launcher - Magazine of 2, comes with another 4. 2x zoom. OHKO
Energy Sword - Infinite ammo. OHKO.
HE Grenade - Find around the map. Depends on range with damage.
Plasma Grenade - Find around the map, sticks to targets. Depends on range with damage.

Current list
Chase (Power 1, Speed 2, Metabolism 2)

This is still in development, sign up and post extra things, I will not include Active Camo, Overshields or any fancy items from Halo 3 in this.

Welcome to The N League II

I haven't hosted a contest for longer than I haven't played N, and that is a hell of a long time. But still doesn't mean to say that this won't be a bad one.

The Rules
  • You need to form a team with another player of the game 'N'. One player must be a mapmaker on the website 'NUMA', the other must be a Highscorer who's name is present on the 'N Highscores Database'.
  • Each team will face another in a series of 'heats' leading to a Quarter Final, Semi Final, and the 'Grande Finale'.
  • If the challenge set isn't completed by one of the teams within the 72hr time limit. The other team will win by Default. If both teams do not enter, they will both be eliminated.
  • The Mapmakers will create to a set criteria each week, as specified by the two judges. The highscorers will try to beat a map from 'NUMA' or randomly from a mappack. Each Highscorer gets 2 attempts, while the Mapmakers get 1 submission.
  • Don't worry, even through there are 8 places on the Tree, more can be added easily.
The Judges
  1. Chase
  2. TBA

#19153 1 2008-02-12T17:26:00Z Chase
All credit for this guide goes to Elwyn from JCXP.net forums. I thought you would all appreciate having the guide here. So I've placed it here. I do not accept any credit for this at all. You can congratulate me all you like, but I won't take any of it.

Quote: Elwyn on JCXP.net
Intro


OK, so I thought Id write a small tutorial for those who dont know how to customise Windows XP.

So you are sick of the plain old boring XP look?
Seeing all the fancy shiny things people are doing in the Desktop Showoff thread?
Wanna know how?

Read on!


Wallpapers

A simple wallpaper change can freshen up your computer to no end.
Some good sites to find wallpapers from:

http://www.deviantart.com/
http://www.studiotwentyeight.com/
http://www.topwalls.com/
http://interfacelift.com

To apply a wallpaper
If the image you are viewing is saved on your computer, Right click on it, and click "Set as Desktop Background"

If the image is in your web browser, right click on it, and click "Use Image on Destop" (or words to that avail!)

Visual Styles

Windows XP has a built in theming engine.
uxtheme.dll is the file in Windows that controls that engine.
By default, uxtheme.dll is locked, so you can not use any non-microsoft skins.
This can be easily unlocked though, either by a application such as StyleXP, or by replacing the uxtheme.dll file with a pre-unlocked one, which I will cover below.

Method one
Using a third party app

Head on over to http://www.stardock.com and see what they have on offer over there.
Although a little costly, and sometimes CPU/RAM intensive, these programs offer the skinning solution for those who do not want to get their hands dirty.

Preparing the System

Method 2
Replacing uxtheme.dll
1)Download the following file,
[attachment=4176:attachment]
(taken from this webpage), or use the program by WindowsX, avaliable here.
2)Unzip it, and run "UXTheme Multi-Patcher 5.0.exe". Follow on screen instructions.

Thats the hard work done!!!!

Finding and Installing Themes


1)Download a theme or visual style you wish to use. Some good sites to get these off include:
http://www.deviantart.com
http://www.themexp.org

2)Extract the downloaded file.
There should be a *.msstyles (eg theme-name.msstyles) file in there somewhere.

3)Browse to C:\WINDOWS\Resources\Themes
(C:\WINDOWS being your windows directory)

4)Create a new folder here, with the same name as the theme file.
For example, if the theme was called 'blah.msstyles', you would create a new folder called 'blah'.

5)Copy the *.msstyles into the folder you just created.
(eg copy 'blah.msstyles' into C:\WINDOWS\Resources\Themes\blah)

To apply your visual style- Go to Display Properties > Appearance > Windows and Buttons, and in the drop down menu, you should see your newly installed visual style


Other Things

There are many other things you can do to customize your desktop, I have just brushed the surface!

Other Apps
There are many third party applications that add usefullness/aesthetics/other to your desktop.
Some of these include:

Sidebars
The Windows Vista sidebar is a popular item to have on your desktop. However it is considered warez to post it, so I will not do that.
There are many free alternatives around, try googling.

Docks
Docks, or custom menus are very popular.
Stardock Objectdock is a shareware application that "lets you organize your short-cuts and running tasks onto an extremely customizable dock that sits on your desktop". A paid version is avaliable with extra features.

Icons
Courtesy of Dragon
Well, you know how "normally" when you want to change you icons, and have the icon pictures, you have to change the icons one by one? Well, I saw many people in many places wanting to change their icons to the popular VISTA icons. So, I found this nifty program that will automate the process for you. Just run this program, and once its completed, all your icons will be VISTA-fied!
Vista Icons Pack v2.1 Ultimate - System Patch


Let your imagination run wild!...


~Elwyn

#19948 1 2008-04-15T15:07:27Z Chase

This is Bungie Studios' answer to the masses, after the giant success of the Heroic Map Pack, they didn't just make one new map, but took 2 old ones and reinvented them to perfection as well. If you wish to watch the ViDoc about it, click this link. Each of these maps comes with a whole host of new stuff in Forge, so that doubles the amount of fun to be had.

Map 1: Ghost Town

Ghost Town is the new map of the trio based on the outskirts of Voi in the Campaign mission Tsavo Highway. There was a campaign to provide the world with water, so you will see the odd pallet of barrels here and there. Each side spawns near a power weapon, one being the Rocket Launcher, the other being the Shotgun, providing a balance, yet neither side of the map is the same, ever.



Map 2: Avalanche

Avalanche is a remake of the Halo: Combat Evolved multiplayer map Sidewinder, I remember this large classic well, with it's Sniper/Shotgun locations right next to each other, literally. I'm sure Bungie swapped those so they aren't next to each other anymore. Also check the size of the Man Cannons here.



Map 3: Blackout

Lockout in Halo 2 makes a proud return in the form of Blackout, and it's been improved in many ways. Why would an oil rig be halfway up an icy mountain? So they put it in an icy ocean, much better located. Each feature sits right where it originally was, spare a jump or two. Meaning those familiar with Lockout should have no problems kicking ass here.



So who isn't hyped for this? It costs 800Gp and there are no discussions of it being free in the future, so I'd not just recommend buying this, but also grabbing a free download of the Heroic maps Standoff, Foundry and Rat's Nest now, as most XBL Playlists require them nowadays.

Zer0, please understand that making a game isn't that simple. You need to learn a programming language, and start from there. Even Game Maker needs you to understand everything about it to make a game in a few weeks or so.

Once you learn a programming language, you have to start with the bare bones of the game (movement, physics, the basic concept of the game). It will take you a while to write that down in the language. Once you're done with that, you can add in levels, sprites, and animations into the game, while going over the programming code again*.

After you've done all of that, congrats. You have just made a basic game. Emphasis on basic. I have no idea how making an online game works, so sorry. So, in conclusion, if you want to make a game, make sure you absolutely want to. You need the patience.

#20183 1 2008-05-08T20:32:05Z Chase


Welcome to MetaFlow

MetaFlow is a project aimed at the whole community, be you talented at image designing or not, this should, in theory, appeal to everybody. I hope you enjoy it almost as much as I did while thinking of the idea.

The main principle behind MetaFlow is that each user submits a 256x256 pixel image, which depicts themselves, each image will, in turn, get a place on the MetaFlow. MetaFlow itself is a cover flow style presentation of these images, similar to Apple's Cover Flow. Where each image will have it's user's name underneath, with the centre image being a MetaFlow starter image, created by me.

So I hope you enjoy the fun, and remember, make sure that the image is you.

Before we begin, I would like to post the necessary rules.
  • The image size must be 256x256px
  • Your entry for the MetaFlow must be sent via PM, Email, or IM to me. I will do the compiling at the end.
  • The order I receive the images in will be the order in the MetaFlow that they will sit. Like this: 864213579 and so on.
  • Each image is also required to have some form of border, do not forget this rule
